submissions.findingTextShort: The 12-RCT/1,140-participant meta-analysis tested multi-herb TCM interventions; it did not test isolated Atractylodes macrocephala.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: PMID 38170849 pooled 12 randomized trials involving 1,140 participants receiving multi-herb traditional Chinese medicine interventions for chronic atrophic gastritis. Atractylodes macrocephala was identified later as one of seven hub herbs through formulation association and network-pharmacology analysis, so the pooled clinical effect and participant count must remain owned by the multi-herb interventions rather than being attributed to isolated Atractylodes.
submissions.populationContext: Participants with chronic atrophic gastritis receiving multi-herb TCM interventions
submissions.usageContext: Combination-formula systematic review/meta-analysis plus network-pharmacology analysis
submissions.uncertaintyNote: The paper supports formulation-level clinical evidence and herb-association context, not Atractylodes monotherapy efficacy.

submissions.findingTextShort: Hub-herb identification by formulation frequency/network pharmacology cannot be promoted into isolated-human efficacy evidence.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: Atractylodes macrocephala appears in the source as a frequently associated hub herb identified through formulation composition and network-pharmacology analysis. That analytic role cannot transfer the meta-analysis effect size, sample size, or evidence strength to Atractylodes as an isolated intervention. Direct proposition-compatible human monotherapy evidence remains separately required.
submissions.populationContext: Evidence-attribution context for a multi-herb clinical literature synthesis
submissions.uncertaintyNote: This correction prevents attribution inflation; it does not establish that Atractylodes has no effects when studied directly.
